- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–15%.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 3–7 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5) and price is trending down, model underestimates support levels; add 2–5% buffer below forecast to avoid undershoot.
- Model frequently overpredicts mid-term (15–30d) trends when sentiment is volatile; use 3-day moving average to dampen noise.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 80+ price spike), model often fails to correct; apply a 10–20% downward adjustment in 10–14 day horizon.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment polarity shift.
